events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.26 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body: This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (Jurong East MRT → NUS), so distance actually driven feeds the fare [F4][F6][RD-2]. The trip ran 14.5 km against an 8.6 km optimal route, +5.9 km, with one off-route segment [F1][F3][RD-1]. The segment 12:12–12:22 drove 6.47 km where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m off route [F3][RD-1]. No exemption applies to that segment: there is no rider-requested stop or named destination [F7][F8][RD-3], no chat in which the driver proposed a route change before leaving the optimal route and the rider agreed [F7][F8][RD-5], and the only traffic data are speed-band records on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (band 4) and JURONG TOWN HALL ROAD (band 5), with no incident recorded near the route [F10][F11][F12]; bands 4–5 are not disqualifying congestion and a speed band alone never exempts under RD-4(b), which the trace also confirms [RD-4]. The driver's statement that his GPS rerouted him is a bare assertion contradicted by the system record and does not supply a "reasonable cause" [F9][F1][F3][RD-4]. Because a non-exempt off-route segment exists, refund_partial applies [RD-2]. Amount = 5.15 km × ($20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.4099/km) = $7.2611, rounded to $7.26 [F3][F6][RD-2], matching the trace formula. The whole-trip billing of $31.56 [F6] is not refunded in full because the base, time and platform components correspond to a completed metered trip; only the extra distance unit generated by the non-exempt detour is recoverable [RD-2]. The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, and this case makes it repeated, so the ruling carries an account review flag [F15][RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your fare for the Jurong East MRT to NUS trip included a detour that wasn't justified. The trip covered 14.5 km against an 8.6 km best route, and one stretch added about 5.15 km while taking you up to roughly 1.2 km off route. No rider-requested stop or agreed route change applies, and the traffic conditions didn't qualify as a reason.

We're refunding $7.26 as a Ryde voucher, covering just the extra distance from that detour — not the base fare for the completed trip. Nothing else is needed from you.

The driver's account is also being sent to Ryde account review.

DRIVER: We reviewed the Jurong East MRT to NUS trip. The route ran 14.5 km against an 8.6 km optimal route, and one segment added about 5.15 km while straying up to roughly 1.2 km off route. No exemption applied: no rider-requested stop or agreed route change, and the recorded traffic conditions don't qualify as a reasonable cause. Your GPS rerouting explanation wasn't supported by the system record.

Outcome: $7.26 of the fare is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher, covering only the extra distance from the off-route segment.

Because this follows earlier upheld route disputes, your account is going to Ryde account review.
